package: W47-02 — reclaim a worktree store lock left by a dead owner
question: Can a worktree ownership-store lock left by a crashed process be reclaimed without weakening mutual exclusion?
answer: Yes, under the recovered pid-reason policy: only a lock whose reason matches the runtime format and names an ESRCH pid is removed, and only after a fresh dev/inode check. Empty, foreign, own-pid and live locks still fail closed.

ranges.role: strict reason regex; own pid and live pid are not releasable; ESRCH decides
reason over 512 bytes or not matching the regex is not stale
sweep: skip current worktree, release-time registry re-read, A1t = 50 cap
kill(pid, 0) reports ESRCH means dead; any other error means not dead

behavior.acquire: write and fsync `harness worktree store (pid N)` into the O_EXCL lock
behavior.reclaim: on EEXIST: open O_NOFOLLOW, require a file of at most 512 bytes, match the runtime reason, require pid in the ported bound and ESRCH, re-stat the same dev/inode, unlink, retry acquisition once
behavior.failClosed: empty, foreign, own-pid, live-pid, out-of-range and identity-changed locks stay and raise the locked error

residuals: A crash between O_EXCL creation and the synchronous reason write leaves a zero-byte lock that fails closed; the recovered client has the same window because it also writes its reason after acquisition.
A pid reused between the crash and reclamation is treated as live; the recovered policy has the same limitation because it checks liveness only.
An own-pid lock is never reclaimed, matching the source; it is released by the owning operation or left until that process exits.
